Prevention: Deep summer ploughing to expose pupae to local predators and reduce pest presence during the growing season.
Synchronous planting of the same variety in endemic locations.
Liberal application of farm yard manure (10 tonnes/acre) or
Conserve and encourage natural enemies like wasps, grasshoppers, ground beetles, spiders, crickets, red ants, coccinellid beetles, ducks and toads.
Avoid using broad-spectrum pesticides as these can harm natural enemies of the pest.
Monitoring: Monitor crops on a weekly basis for pests and signs of infestation.
Symptoms include brown discoloration of leaves, wounds and lesions present on leaves.
Affected crops may turn reddish brown or yellow in colour.
Bugs are more active during full moon week.
Installation of light traps (1 per acre) to catch adults.
Consider direct control actions awhen 2-3 bugs are found per 10 randomly monitored crops.
Direct Control: Beauveria bassiana at a rate of 800 g per acre.
Breed ducks as they feed on black bugs.
Draining of water and spraying of neem oil 3% (6 litres per acre) on 30, 45 and 60 days after transplanting.
Spraying of 200 ml of 0.05% soap solution (a mixture of 0.5 g all-purpose detergent in 1 litre of water).
Instalation of fish meal trap at a rate of 5 nos per acre.
Flooding the field periodically to drown the bugs.
During early infestation, raise the water level in the field for 2−3 days to force the insects to move upwards (more likely to be killed by natural enemies).
Restrictions: Always wear protective clothing when handling pesticides.
